# E0340: polymorphic function type out of place

A generic function type is only the type of a parameter or a field. Return a function of known types, as `fn(i64) -> i64`, or make the outer function generic.

- Rule: [`polymorphism.placement`](../../reference/07-types.md#polymorphism.placement)
- Reported at: the polymorphic function type.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0340:1
fn make() -> fn<T>(T) -> T { |x| x }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn make() -> fn(i64) -> i64 { |x| x }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0340_polymorphic_function_type_out_of_place.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0340_polymorphic_function_type_out_of_place.lt):

```text
── POLYMORPHIC FUNCTION TYPE OUT OF PLACE ── E0340_polymorphic_function_type_out_of_place.lt:1:14  [E0340]

A polymorphic function type can't be a result; only a parameter, a field or a
payload can have one:

  1 │ fn make() -> fn<T>(T) -> T { |x| x }
    │              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^

A generic function type is only the type of a parameter or a field. Return a
function of known types, as `fn(i64) -> i64`, or make the outer function
generic.
```
